comparison_summary: Supragingival scaling (ST) vs supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing (IT) in T2DM patients with chronic severe periodontitis
intervention_description: Supragingival scaling using an ultrasonic device and periodontal curettes (Hu-Friedy®, Chicago, USA). A single appointment lasted ~60 minutes. Supportive therapy for biofilm control consisted of professional instructions on oral hygiene given to each patient every month.

comparison_summary: Supragingival scaling (ST) vs supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing (IT) in T2DM patients with chronic severe periodontitis
intervention_description: Supra- and subgingival scaling and root planing (in sites with PPD ≥ 4 mm) using an ultrasonic device and periodontal curettes (Hu-Friedy®, Chicago, USA). Procedures performed under local anesthesia (3% prilocaine with felypressin), in two appointments lasting ~120 minutes each. Supportive therapy for biofilm control consisted of professional instructions on oral hygiene given to each patient every month.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment + subgingival debridement vs non-surgical periodontal treatment + supragingival prophylaxis vs no treatment control
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal treatment (scaling and root planing under local anesthesia) at baseline and additional subgingival debridement at the 3-month follow-up, completed within 24 hours by an experienced periodontist without antibiotics or local antimicrobials, using standard rigid periodontal curets and ultrasonic instrumentation. Oral hygiene instructions reinforced at each visit.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment + subgingival debridement vs non-surgical periodontal treatment + supragingival prophylaxis vs no treatment control
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal treatment (scaling and root planing under local anesthesia) at baseline and only supragingival prophylaxis with no intervention in deep periodontal pockets at 3 months, completed within 24 hours by an experienced periodontist without antibiotics or local antimicrobials, using standard rigid periodontal curets and ultrasonic instrumentation. Oral hygiene instructions reinforced at each visit.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment + subgingival debridement vs non-surgical periodontal treatment + supragingival prophylaxis vs no treatment control
intervention_description: No treatment measure or formal oral hygiene instructions until the end of the study.

comparison_summary: Tooth extraction alone vs tooth extraction + FM-SRP in T2DM patients and non-diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted from each patient. Control group did not receive any other treatment until the 3-month follow-up.

arm_label: Tooth Extraction and Periodontal Treatment (FM-SRP) (T2DM treatment group)
comparison_summary: Tooth extraction alone vs tooth extraction + FM-SRP in T2DM patients and non-diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted. Prior to surgical procedures, Full-Mouth Scaling and Root Planing (FM-SRP) using an ultrasonic device (UDS-J Ultrasonic Scaler, Guilin Woodpecker Medical Instrument) and periodontal curettes for mechanical debridement of supra- and subgingival plaque and calculus. Post-operative rinsing with antiseptic solution Listerine® (ethanol 21.6%, methyl salicylate 0.06%, menthol 0.042%, thymol 0.064% and eucalyptol 0.092%) as a mouthwash thrice a day for 3 weeks.

comparison_summary: Tooth extraction alone vs tooth extraction + FM-SRP in T2DM patients and non-diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted from each patient. Non-diabetic control group did not receive any other treatment (FM-SRP) until the 3-month follow-up.

arm_label: Tooth Extraction and Periodontal Treatment (FM-SRP) (Non-Diabetic treatment group)
comparison_summary: Tooth extraction alone vs tooth extraction + FM-SRP in T2DM patients and non-diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: At least one tooth was extracted. Prior to surgical procedures, Full-Mouth Scaling and Root Planing (FM-SRP) using an ultrasonic device (UDS-J Ultrasonic Scaler, Guilin Woodpecker Medical Instrument) and periodontal curettes for mechanical debridement of supra- and subgingival plaque and calculus. Post-operative rinsing with antiseptic solution Listerine® as a mouthwash thrice a day for 3 weeks.

comparison_summary: SRP alone vs SRP + doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions and full mouth scaling and root planing (SRP)

comparison_summary: SRP alone vs SRP + doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions and full mouth SRP plus doxycycline (DOXT, Dr Reddy's Lab. Ltd, Hyderabad, India) (total dose 1,600 mg in equally divided 16 doses, start as 100 mg BD followed by OD for 14 days)

comparison_summary: SRP alone vs SRP + doxycycline vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment until 3 months (control); all control group subjects were treated with required periodontal intervention after the final assessment of study parameters after 3 months.

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP + chlorhexidine rinse) vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Initial treatment consisted of at least 160 minutes of scaling and root planing using currettes and ultrasonic instruments with local anesthesia during 2 or more sessions completed within 42 days of the baseline visit. After treatment, the therapist provided oral hygiene instructions and dispensed chlorhexidine gluconate (0.12% oral rinse, twice daily for 2 weeks), toothbrush, toothpaste, and dental floss. Three and 6 months after the baseline visit, participants in the treatment group received oral hygiene instructions and scaling and root planing for approximately 1 hour during a single session.

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP + chlorhexidine rinse) vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Participants in the control group received only oral hygiene instructions at the baseline and 3- and 6-month visits. Following their 6-month visit, control group participants were offered scaling and root planing.

comparison_summary: Immediate non-surgical periodontal therapy (SRP + systemic antibiotics + OHI) vs delayed periodontal therapy (no active treatment during follow-up)
intervention_description: Full-mouth SRP performed in a single two-hour session using ultrasonic apparatus (Cavitron Select SPC, Dentsply professional) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy), with local anesthesia when needed. SRP associated with subgingival irrigation by chlorhexidine 0.12% mouthwash (Peridex oral rinse, 3M ESPE). Immediately after SRP, systemic antibiotics commenced: metronidazole 400 mg three times daily for two weeks and amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 2 weeks. Oral hygiene instructions (OHI) provided. Patients received free dental care products necessary for periodontal maintenance during follow-up.

comparison_summary: Immediate non-surgical periodontal therapy (SRP + systemic antibiotics + OHI) vs delayed periodontal therapy (no active treatment during follow-up)
intervention_description: No periodontal therapies during the follow-up period. Delayed periodontal therapy was performed using the same procedures as the test group exactly after the end of the follow-up period (3 months) for ethical reasons.

comparison_summary: Intensive periodontal treatment (IPT) vs control periodontal treatment (CPT) in patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate-to-severe periodontitis
intervention_description: Patients in the IPT group received an initial single session of whole mouth scaling of the root surfaces under local analgesia, with no time limit set for the duration of the session. 2 months after the first whole mouth scaling session, patients with good oral hygiene (dental plaque scores of ≤20%) and at least one 6 mm or deeper residual periodontal pocket had periodontal surgical therapy to improve access for root surface cleaning. Patients who still had suboptimum oral hygiene or did not have residual 6 mm or deeper periodontal pockets at 2 months received additional scaling of the root surfaces under local analgesia. All patients in the IPT group subsequently received further sessions of scaling of the root surfaces under local analgesia every 3 months until completion of the study.

comparison_summary: Intensive periodontal treatment (IPT) vs control periodontal treatment (CPT) in patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate-to-severe periodontitis
intervention_description: Patients in the CPT group received supra-gingival scaling and polishing of all dentition at the same time-points as the IPT group (after baseline and at 2, 6, 9, and 12 months after the completion of the first session of periodontal therapy). At the end of the study, patients in the CPT group received any additional periodontal therapy that was required.

comparison_summary: SRP plus oral hygiene instructions vs oral hygiene instructions alone
intervention_description: Scaling and root planing performed with an ultrasonic scaler (Dentsply, York, PA, USA) and Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, IL, USA). Two quadrants were instrumented at each appointment under local anaesthesia, using 2% lidocaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine (Dentsply), with an endpoint of achieving smooth root surfaces. The procedure was performed by two calibrated periodontists. Oral hygiene instructions including the modified Bass technique, use of inter-proximal toothbrushes and dental floss were also provided.

comparison_summary: SRP plus oral hygiene instructions vs oral hygiene instructions alone
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions only, including the modified Bass technique, use of inter-proximal toothbrushes and dental floss. No professional subgingival instrumentation was performed during the study period.

comparison_summary: Early Treatment (periodontal scaling and root planing plus doxycycline and chlorhexidine) vs Usual Care (no active periodontal treatment) over 4 months
intervention_description: Early Treatment for 4 months (periodontal scaling and root planing until smooth root surfaces were achieved plus doxycycline [100 mg by mouth daily for 14 days] and chlorhexidine gluconate [CHX] rinses [30 cc, 0.12%, twice daily for 4 months]), then Usual Care.

comparison_summary: Early Treatment (periodontal scaling and root planing plus doxycycline and chlorhexidine) vs Usual Care (no active periodontal treatment) over 4 months
intervention_description: Usual Care — participants did not alter their medical and dental care routine; rather, they proceeded with their health care as usual. For some this meant that they used dental and medical services, for others it did not.

comparison_summary: Full-mouth scaling and root planing vs no periodontal treatment in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients
intervention_description: Full-mouth scaling and root planing performed under local anaesthesia, plus oral hygiene instructions. Patients also received extractions or root canal treatment for teeth with periapical lesions as needed.

comparison_summary: Full-mouth scaling and root planing vs no periodontal treatment in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment during the study period. After completion of the study, these patients were given a full non-surgical and supportive periodontal treatment if needed.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal therapy (immediate) vs untreated control (delayed intervention)
intervention_description: Full-mouth non-surgical periodontal therapy comprising supra- and subgingival scaling using Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, USA), and piezoelectric ultrasonic device (Kyungwon Ferrite, Gyeonggi-Do, South Korea) with universal tips. Full-mouth dental prophylaxis using a rubber cup and Ainsworth prophylaxis paste to remove plaque and tooth stains. Local anaesthesia administered as required. All participants received oral hygiene advice consisting of toothbrush and flossing instructions and were provided with a toothbrush and toothpaste at baseline. Single untimed session (ranging from 45 min up to 3 h).

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal therapy (immediate) vs untreated control (delayed intervention)
intervention_description: Untreated control; periodontal intervention was delayed for 12 months in those randomized to the control group. All participants received oral hygiene advice consisting of toothbrush and flossing instructions and were provided with a toothbrush and toothpaste at baseline.

comparison_summary: Anti-infectious periodontal treatment (SRP + topical minocycline) vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Mechanical debridement of the sub-gingival plaque and calculus was performed using piezo-electric ultra sonic scalers, and 10 mg of minocycline ointment (Periofil®, Showa Yakuhin Co., Tokyo, Japan) was administered topically in every periodontal pocket at the end of each visit. The intensive periodontal treatment was completed over the course of four visits within 2 months. After completion, additional periodontal treatment including instructions for brushing, supra- and sub-gingival debridement without topical administration of antibiotics were performed if necessary.

comparison_summary: Anti-infectious periodontal treatment (SRP + topical minocycline) vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Control group participants received instructions for brushing their teeth, including the use of inter-proximal cleaning aids, such as floss and inter-dental brushes, depending on their individual needs.

comparison_summary: CRP-decreased subgroup vs CRP-unchanged or increased subgroup within the intervention group
intervention_description: Subgroup of intervention arm in which serum hs-CRP decreased at 1 month following periodontal treatment. Received same treatment as intervention group: mechanical debridement using piezo-electric ultrasonic scalers plus topical minocycline ointment 10 mg in every periodontal pocket, completed over four visits within 2 months.

comparison_summary: CRP-decreased subgroup vs CRP-unchanged or increased subgroup within the intervention group
intervention_description: Subgroup of intervention arm in which serum hs-CRP was unchanged or increased at 1 month following periodontal treatment. Received same treatment as intervention group: mechanical debridement using piezo-electric ultrasonic scalers plus topical minocycline ointment 10 mg in every periodontal pocket, completed over four visits within 2 months.

comparison_summary: SRP (scaling and root planing) vs supragingival prophylaxis (delayed treatment control)
intervention_description: Full-mouth scaling and root planing (SRP) in two sessions, 1 week apart, with the use of an ultrasonic scaler (Minipiezon Electromedical Systems EMS, Nyon, Switzerland) and hand instruments, under local anaesthesia. Additional supportive SRP at each visit if judged necessary. Oral hygiene instructions after each visit.

comparison_summary: SRP (scaling and root planing) vs supragingival prophylaxis (delayed treatment control)
intervention_description: Periodontal prophylaxis at baseline in the form of supragingival removal of all deposits (plaque and calculus) with an ultrasonic scaler. SRP was performed in the CG after the completion of the study (after the 6-month visit). Oral hygiene instructions after each visit.

comparison_summary: SRP + OHI (TG/GT) vs supragingival scaling + OHI (CG/GC) in type 2 diabetes patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions (modified Bass technique) + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus using an ultrasonic scaler (Satelec P5 Newtron XS, Acteon, Merignac, France). Oral hygiene instructions were repeated at 3 and 6 month control visits.

comparison_summary: SRP + OHI (TG/GT) vs supragingival scaling + OHI (CG/GC) in type 2 diabetes patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions (modified Bass technique) + supragingival removal of plaque and calculus using an ultrasonic scaler (Satelec P5 Newtron XS) + full-mouth debridement consisting of scaling and root planing (SRP) using ultrasound and Gracey curettes. At 3-month visit, OHI repeated and SRP reviewed; additional mouth debridement conducted when needed (presence of bleeding points and/or increased PPD).

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP) vs no treatment in T2DM patients with good or poor glycemic control, and vs nondiabetic controls receiving SRP
intervention_description: Nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy Manufacturing Co.) and an ultrasonic scaler (Suprasson P5 Booster, Satelec-Acteon group., Merignac, France). Oral hygiene instructions were given at baseline and reviewed at each visit; additional supportive SRP was done when necessary.

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP) vs no treatment in T2DM patients with good or poor glycemic control, and vs nondiabetic controls receiving SRP
intervention_description: Nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy Manufacturing Co.) and an ultrasonic scaler (Suprasson P5 Booster, Satelec-Acteon group., Merignac, France). Oral hygiene instructions were given at baseline and reviewed at each visit; additional supportive SRP was done when necessary.

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP) vs no treatment in T2DM patients with good or poor glycemic control, and vs nondiabetic controls receiving SRP
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment during the study period. Periodontal treatment was performed in the no-treatment group (NT group) after completion of the study (after 6 months).

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP) vs no treatment in T2DM patients with good or poor glycemic control, and vs nondiabetic controls receiving SRP
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment during the study period. Periodontal treatment was performed in the no-treatment group (NT group) after completion of the study (after 6 months).

comparison_summary: Nonsurgical periodontal therapy (SRP) vs no treatment in T2DM patients with good or poor glycemic control, and vs nondiabetic controls receiving SRP
intervention_description: Nonsurgical periodontal treatment comprising four SRP sessions over a maximum of 2 weeks, using standard rigid Gracey curettes (Hu-Friedy Manufacturing Co.) and an ultrasonic scaler (Suprasson P5 Booster, Satelec-Acteon group., Merignac, France). Oral hygiene instructions were given at baseline and reviewed at each visit; additional supportive SRP was done when necessary.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment (SRP + oral hygiene instructions) vs oral hygiene instructions only (control)
intervention_description: Participants in the control group received only oral hygiene instructions at the baseline and 3 and 6 month visits. Initially, all participants received one session of supra-gingival plaque removal and oral hygiene instructions. After the study completion, the control group participants received scaling and root planing.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment (SRP + oral hygiene instructions) vs oral hygiene instructions only (control)
intervention_description: Non-surgical periodontal treatment consisting of at least 60 minutes of scaling and root planing using curettes (BioGent Curette, Hu-Friedy; Scaler YB, YDM Corporation) and an ultrasonic instrument (Varios 750, NSK) during 2 or more sessions completed within 42 days after the baseline visit. Therapists provided oral hygiene instructions, professional toothbrushing and mechanical tooth cleaning during treatment. Three and 6 months after baseline, participants received periodontal maintenance therapy including oral hygiene instructions and oral prophylaxis for approximately 1 hour during a single session. Initially, all participants received one session of supra-gingival plaque removal and oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT (SRP with additional toothbrushing) vs CTR (control) in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: After a baseline oral examination, oral health education including toothbrush instruction was conducted. Supragingival scaling was performed only on the first visit by 2 trained dentists working together simultaneously. After 2 weeks, root planing was performed to remove the subgingival calculus. At 12 weeks, patients were recalled to re-check their oral health status. If they required additional periodontal treatment, it was done at 12 weeks.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT (SRP with additional toothbrushing) vs CTR (control) in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: After a baseline oral examination, oral health education including toothbrush instruction was conducted. In the SRPAT group, additional toothbrushing (Watanabe method) with a 2-row toothbrush was applied on the first visit by a trained dentist. On the second visit, subgingival calculus was removed as appropriate according to the patient's oral health condition. Additional toothbrushing (Watanabe method) was performed once a week from the first visit through the fifth visit.

comparison_summary: SRP vs SRPAT (SRP with additional toothbrushing) vs CTR (control) in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: The CTR group received no other treatments beyond medical screening for diabetes. However, all groups received oral health education including toothbrush instruction at the baseline visit to eliminate intergroup bias associated with routine oral health behaviours. After the study was completed, the necessary dental treatment was provided to the patients who wished to receive it.

comparison_summary: SRP + MET + OHI vs SRP + OHI vs OHI only (control)
intervention_description: Participants of test group-1 received SRP through a combination of ultrasonic scaling (average 60 min on medium intensity full mouth in single sitting) and hand instrumentation (using sharpened and sterilized curettes) to smoothen irregular areas of root surface until the surfaces were smooth followed by MET 400 mg × 3 for 10 days along with warm salt water rinses for 3–5 days and OHI.

comparison_summary: SRP + MET + OHI vs SRP + OHI vs OHI only (control)
intervention_description: Participants in test group-2 received the same intervention as test group-1 except MET: SRP through a combination of ultrasonic scaling and hand instrumentation along with warm salt water rinses for 3–5 days and OHI.

comparison_summary: SRP + MET + OHI vs SRP + OHI vs OHI only (control)
intervention_description: The control-group received only OHI and was provided periodontal therapy at end of trial.

comparison_summary: NSPT vs OHI in Type 2 diabetes subjects with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Full mouth debridement consisting of scaling and root planing done in a single visit using an ultrasonic scaler (SATELEC P5 Newtron XS) and Gracey curettes; additionally, 0.12% Chlorhexidine mouthrinse (Hexipro®) three times a day using 15 ml each time for 14 days. All subjects also received oral hygiene instructions using a soft bristled toothbrush, compact-tuft toothbrush, interdental brushes and dental floss (TePe® oral hygiene education set) with modified Bass technique. Plaque scores reviewed at weekly intervals to achieve ≤20%. At each monthly recall visit, subjects received professional prophylaxis comprising scaling and polishing.

comparison_summary: NSPT vs OHI in Type 2 diabetes subjects with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instructions and motivation only, using a soft bristled toothbrush, compact-tuft toothbrush, interdental brushes and dental floss (TePe® oral hygiene education set) with modified Bass technique. No interventional treatment was given apart from oral hygiene instructions and motivation. At each monthly recall visit, participants were reviewed and re-motivated.

comparison_summary: SRP alone vs SRP plus systemic doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Full mouth scaling and root planing under local anesthesia, with oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: SRP alone vs SRP plus systemic doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: Full mouth scaling and root planing under local anesthesia plus oral hygiene instructions, with systemic doxycycline 100 mg (DOXY-1, USV Pharmaceuticals), two tablets on the first day followed by one tablet daily for 14 days.

comparison_summary: SRP alone vs SRP plus systemic doxycycline vs no treatment (control)
intervention_description: No oral hygiene instructions and no full mouth scaling and root planing performed.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment (immediate) vs delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Scaling and root planing performed under local anesthesia, divided in four sessions within 24 h, each of 45 min per quadrant, using an ultrasonic scaler (PIEZO-soft ultrasonic scaler; KaVo Dental, Germany) equipped with PIEZO Scaler Tip 201, and manual instruments (Gracey Curettes, SG 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, 11/12, 13/14; Gracey Curette, SAS 3/4, 11/12, 13/14; Hu-Friedy, USA). Ultrasonic instrumentation performed in apical to cervical direction using linear oscillations at 30 KHz with medium power setting. A continuous water spray and subgingival irrigation with antiseptic mouthwash (chlorhexidine 0.12%) was associated. Preceded by motivational intervention and customized oral hygiene instructions.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal treatment (immediate) vs delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Delayed non-surgical periodontal treatment; no active periodontal treatment during the 6-month follow-up period. At the end of the 6-month follow-up period the non-surgical periodontal treatment was carried out for the control group, performing the same procedures as the intervention group, for ethical reasons.

comparison_summary: Periodontal intervention (SRP + surgery + antibiotics) vs no periodontal intervention in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: No periodontal intervention. Blood samples were taken at baseline and after 3 months without periodontal intervention.

comparison_summary: Periodontal intervention (SRP + surgery + antibiotics) vs no periodontal intervention in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Periodontal intervention included oral hygiene, full-mouth scaling (supragingival and subgingival scaling), root planning, periodontal flap surgery when indicated, and extraction of hopeless teeth, restore of balanced occlusion. Antibiotics (Tinidazole 1.0 g, bid, po. and ampicillin 0.25 g, qid, po.) were prescribed for 3 days before and after periodontal intervention. All periodontal interventions were performed by one periodontist.

comparison_summary: Scaling + mouthwash + brushing vs mouthwash + brushing vs brushing only in type 2 diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: Patients who had undergone scaling, were advised to regularly use 0.12% mouthwash (once daily) and brush (twice daily)

comparison_summary: Scaling + mouthwash + brushing vs mouthwash + brushing vs brushing only in type 2 diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: Patients who were advised to regularly use 0.12% chlorhexidine mouthwash (once daily) and brush (twice daily)

comparison_summary: Scaling + mouthwash + brushing vs mouthwash + brushing vs brushing only in type 2 diabetic patients with periodontitis
intervention_description: Patients who were advised to brush (twice daily)

comparison_summary: Immediate periodontal treatment (SRP + systemic antibiotics + OHI) vs delayed periodontal treatment (no treatment control)
intervention_description: Full-mouth non-surgical scaling and root planing (SRP) performed in a single 2-hr session using full-mouth ultrasonic and hand instrument debridement, with local anaesthesia if necessary, subgingival irrigation with antiseptic mouthwash (chlorhexidine 0.12%), systemic antibiotics (amoxicillin 2 g/day for 7 days after periodontal treatment), personalized oral health instructions (OHI), and a free pack of dental care products for 3 months of periodontal maintenance. SRP was performed over the 10-day period following the inclusion visit.

comparison_summary: Immediate periodontal treatment (SRP + systemic antibiotics + OHI) vs delayed periodontal treatment (no treatment control)
intervention_description: Delayed periodontal treatment: no periodontal procedure was performed during the 3-month follow-up period. The same periodontal treatment procedures as the intervention group were performed at the end of the 3-month follow-up period for ethical reasons. Therefore, the control group was a true 'no treatment' control arm.

comparison_summary: Periodontal therapy vs no intervention in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: All subjects in the intervention group underwent a periodontal intervention that included oral hygiene (utilizing correct methods and soft-bristled toothbrushes, interdental brushes and dental floss), full-mouth scaling (supragingival and subgingival scaling), the extraction of hopeless teeth, and the restoration of balanced occlusion. All periodontal interventions were completed by a single periodontist (Jingsong Liu) within two weeks.

comparison_summary: Periodontal therapy vs no intervention in T2DM patients with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: No periodontal intervention; no changes in medications or diet were made during the study period.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal therapy plus OHI vs OHI alone in T2DM patients with moderate to severe chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instruction (OHI), scaling and root debridement with both hand instruments and ultrasonic scaler, extraction of hopeless teeth. Review appointments given every 4–6 weeks to reinforce patients' plaque control.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal therapy plus OHI vs OHI alone in T2DM patients with moderate to severe chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Oral hygiene instruction (OHI) alone. Similar periodontal treatment provided after completion of the study.

comparison_summary: Immediate NSPT (scaling, root planing + subgingival povidone iodine irrigation) vs delayed periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Immediate full mouth debridement in a single visit consisting of scaling, root scaling and planning using a magneto-restrictive ultrasonic device (Denjoy Dus-1A) and Gracey's cures, followed by sub-gingival irrigation with 10% povidone iodine solution. Additionally, subjects received dental floss and chlorhexidine gluconate 0.2% mouthwash (10 ml twice daily for 5 days). All subjects were instructed in oral hygiene methods using modified Bass technique and soft bristled toothbrush. At recall visit 6 months after enrolment, a professional prophylaxis including scaling and polishing was performed.

comparison_summary: Immediate NSPT (scaling, root planing + subgingival povidone iodine irrigation) vs delayed periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: No interventional periodontal treatment was given during the follow-up, apart from oral hygiene instructions. Participants received the same standardized education session on diabetes management and dental hygiene. At the end of the study, all participants in the control group received the same treatment as the treatment group (delayed periodontal treatment).

comparison_summary: SRP (treatment) vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: Patients in the treatment group underwent oral health instructions, supra-/subgingival scaling (Cavitron Bobcat Pro, Dentsply, York, PA, USA), and manual curettage (Hu-Friedy, Chicago, IL, USA), which were completed within 2 weeks after the baseline evaluation.

comparison_summary: SRP (treatment) vs no periodontal treatment (control)
intervention_description: The control group was not given any periodontal treatment except for evaluations at the baseline as well as on the 3rd and 6th months.

comparison_summary: ERP (sub-ERP) vs prophylaxis (subprophylaxis) after initial SRP
intervention_description: Patients in the sub-ERP group again received full-month ultrasonic scaling and manual root planing of the teeth with PPD ≥ 4 mm.

comparison_summary: ERP (sub-ERP) vs prophylaxis (subprophylaxis) after initial SRP
intervention_description: The subprophylaxis group received only full-month ultrasonic scaling to remove calculus and plaque.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal therapy (SRP + doxycycline) vs no periodontal treatment (doxycycline only) in type 2 diabetics with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Scaling and root planning (subgingival scaling and root planning under topical anesthesia on a quadrant-by-quadrant basis, preceded by intensive oral health instruction and supragingival scaling and polishing) plus doxycycline 100 mg/day for 14 days.

comparison_summary: Non-surgical periodontal therapy (SRP + doxycycline) vs no periodontal treatment (doxycycline only) in type 2 diabetics with chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: No periodontal treatment (control group) for the duration of the study, plus doxycycline 100 mg/day for 14 days. Patients were then treated in the same manner as group A after the study period.

comparison_summary: Surgical periodontal therapy (modified Widman flap) vs supportive periodontal therapy (SRP + chlorhexidine rinse) in chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Modified Widman flap procedures performed in areas with deep pockets: reverse incisions, full thickness mucoperiosteal flaps raised, granulation tissue removed, root instrumentation performed, alveolar bone shape corrected; flaps replaced and sutured, sutures removed 1 week post-surgery.

comparison_summary: Surgical periodontal therapy (modified Widman flap) vs supportive periodontal therapy (SRP + chlorhexidine rinse) in chronic periodontitis
intervention_description: Scaling and root planning on diseased root surfaces; subjects advised to rinse with 0.2% chlorhexidine solution twice daily for 2 weeks.
